sentence: This project studies the role of a nuclear hormone receptor in making arterial, venous and lymphatic endothelium, and how its activity is controlled.
This project uses cell culture models to find out how the development of the placenta is disrupted in preeclampsia.
This project studies the receptor that platelets use to bind clotting proteins and the receptor that activates platelets through immune complexes.
This project tries to find out how retinal immune cells add to blood vessel and nerve cell damage in a retinopathy, using mouse models.
This project uses single molecule measurements to study the structure and energy of RNA and how it interacts with ligands.
This project uses brain imaging, including MRI scans of brains from donors, to study how Alzheimer’s disease progresses.
This project uses statistical genetics, machine learning and functional genomics to find genes in one region of human DNA that drive disease risk.
This project studies treatments that target how the mitochondrial network changes in acute respiratory distress syndrome.
This project tries to find out what causes changes in microflora in chronic kidney disease and whether they make the disease worse.
This project studies how a type of immune cell called innate lymphoid cells changes its type during infection and inflammation of the gut.
This project uses artificial intelligence and CT scans to measure damage to the aortic valve and predict the risk of death or stroke.
This project builds and tests a digital sleep program for families of young children with sleep problems.
This project studies how to push embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma cells to mature and stop growing, using mouse and zebrafish models.
This project studies how short and long noncoding RNAs help herpesviruses stay latent and cause tumors.
This project tests whether a drug can restore healthy cell adhesion and stop harmful movement of vascular smooth muscle cells.
This project builds human gut-liver models made of primary cells to study how the two organs affect each other's cells.
This project builds and runs computer systems that manage data for research projects, including patient reported outcomes and pathology and biomarker data.
This project studies the types of DNA replication stress in cancer cells and how RNA affects DNA replication and repair.
This project adapts a brain imaging method called hemogenetic imaging to measure brain-wide function in primates from genetically targeted cell types.
This project develops deep learning tools to diagnose retinopathy of prematurity from images, using animal-to-human translated images and multi-task learning.
